projects.title: Relay
projects.subtitle: Voice-first employee service, carried through to a verified result
projects.narration: At most companies, HR, IT, payroll and learning each run their own portal, with their own forms and owners. New hires have to work out which system, form and person applies, and support teams untangle requests that arrive incomplete or at the wrong desk. Relay puts all of it in one workspace, with a voice agent built on Deepgram that connects every service to a single conversation. Here’s Maya, a new hire, on day one. It reads Maya’s own records, picks the task due first, and opens the exact form, ready to start. Raising a concern works the same way: Relay drafts a complete IT request for the right team and files it when Maya confirms. It books meetings on the calendar and explains what’s holding up a first paycheck, and every action waits for the employee’s click. Underneath, an intelligence layer built for Relay gives the agent a small set of tools to read records, open them, highlight sections and propose actions. The agent only names the record; Relay works out the page and the highlight itself, and refuses any target it doesn’t recognize. The server decides who is signed in and gives the agent that employee’s records alone, so each person reaches only what they’re authorized to see. Sensitive details, like bank numbers, are removed before the agent ever sees them. HR and IT see a timeline of every request, from what was asked to the verified change. On the real app, 103 of 110 conversations ended fully right, and 31 of 34 spoken requests got a useful answer. It stops talking within 51 milliseconds when the employee cuts in, and red-team attacks caused no unsafe actions. Whatever the request, the employee says it once, and Relay finds the record, the owner and the next step.

projects.title: Refract
projects.subtitle: One research session connecting papers, evidence, analysis, and decisions
projects.narration: Research arguments are assembled across PDF readers, AI chats, notebooks, and spreadsheets, and each transfer can detach a claim from its source. Refract makes one persistent research session the continuity layer. In the Reader, a selected passage can be explained, summarised, quizzed, or saved, and every grounded answer keeps its page and chunk. Index and Compare turn that evidence into concept memory, cross-paper comparisons, and a coverage map that exposes gaps before writing begins. A React front end calls a Fast API service, with Postgres for sessions, Chroma DB for retrieval, and Claude for grounded synthesis. Stats moves a dataset through ordered checkpoints: profile, audit, and baseline regression. Each column receives an analytical role, and Spearman screening flags leakage and redundancy before any model trains. In a battery remaining-useful-life case study, cycle index was flagged as leakage and excluded through a saved decision, and models were compared on a fixed split and seed. Interpretive claims carry one of five provenance labels, and anything unlabelled stays unresolved. What makes Refract distinctive is the preserved chain: paper, passage, question, dataset, feature decision, model, and metric stay connected in one session.

projects.title: Homeward
projects.subtitle: Source-linked recovery planning after hospital discharge
projects.narration: Discharge instructions arrive when patients are exhausted, and one unclear line can stall recovery. Homeward turns the saved record into a plan Alex can follow. View source opens the exact sentence behind each step. Alex asks what paperwork to bring, and source search answers with the cited passage. The lab instruction names no test or date, so Alex asks for help. The care team replies, and the task stays open until the details are confirmed. A reminder waits for Alex's approval. When the response is lost, Retry safely returns the original receipt, so no second reminder appears. The agent activity log records every step. Four role-scoped specialists select references, and the server validates patient, record version, and approval. All 32 guardrail checks pass, alongside 59 backend tests and four interface journeys. Uncertainty stays visible, and every instruction keeps its source.

projects.title: Birb Hangout
projects.subtitle: A shared 3D place for the quiet rituals of friendship
projects.narration: Most remote social products demand a conversation or a shared game. Birb Hangout was built for the quieter rituals that make physical presence comfortable: reading while a friend chooses music, resting by the fire, watching together, sharing a hug, or taking flight. Friends enter a private 3D lounge as birds, and the room itself becomes the interface. Records, books, television, trivia, gestures, and furniture make activities visible and easy to join. Resting by the fire opens into a shared Dream where momentum-driven flight crosses rivers, forests, and floating islands. The engineering matches synchronization to each social behavior, from authoritative room state to peer voice and staged interactions. Its special contribution extends into development: specialist studios preserve camera, scene state, and spatial annotations so visual feedback becomes reproducible evidence for animation and world design.

projects.title: TraceLens
projects.subtitle: Measuring the action a health-information answer ultimately gives
projects.narration: Someone asks a chatbot about a friend slurring words and drifting in and out of consciousness after a hot tub. The answer calls it heat exhaustion, suggests care within one to two hours, and keeps 911 for if the friend loses consciousness. A physician labelled this case an emergency, and the answer was read as self-care. That gap is under-triage. TraceLens sends the same message to Vega, a decision model that reads only the person’s words. At the median, Gemma takes 67 seconds per answer, and Vega decides in 0.36 seconds without writing a word. Vega scores this message 0.98, above its frozen threshold, so the disagreement is shown to the person. The chatbot reconsiders and now says to call emergency services immediately, with its first answer still visible. The research runs in one workspace: saved runs and receipts, blinded review, gate decisions, and Colab training. On held-out cases, Vega reached an AUC of 0.966. Replaying 277 saved cases, Vega flagged 18 of 31 missed emergencies, and emergency guidance rose from 39 to 47 of 70. False alarms went from four to five of 134.

projects.title: Brain Atrophy Analysis in Dementia
projects.subtitle: An interpretable OpenCV measurement published through IEEE
projects.narration: Measuring brain atrophy from MRI can require expert tracing and time-consuming segmentation. This study asked whether visible tissue loss, ventricular expansion, and widened sulci could become a repeatable image-level measure. The OpenCV workflow separates dark space, bright tissue, and mid-range tissue, then computes an auditable ratio: black pixels divided by white plus grey pixels. Across 2,198 ADNI T1-weighted MRI images, cohort averages established lower and upper reference bounds of 0.41 and 0.83. The same method was evaluated with two anatomical views. Focusing the crop around the hippocampal region improved reported accuracy from 66 to 71 percent. The work is distinctive because the anatomical hypothesis, pixel masks, equation, reference bounds, and crop comparison remain visible from input image to result, creating an interpretable computer-vision pipeline that was published in the IEEE ICRITO 2022 proceedings.

projects.title: Four-Class Alzheimer MRI Classification
projects.subtitle: A notebook-first TensorFlow experiment with probability ensembling
projects.narration: Four-class Alzheimer MRI classification must separate adjacent stages whose scans can look structurally similar. This experiment turns 6,400 folder-labelled MRI images into a complete TensorFlow workflow. It inspects the scans, builds an 80-10-10 train, validation, and test pipeline, resizes images to 256 square pixels, and applies augmentation only to training data. The primary convolutional network contains six convolution-and-pooling blocks, dropout, a dense representation, and a four-class softmax output. Independently saved models are then compared through their full probability vectors, allowing uncertain judgments to be combined before the final class is chosen. In the author-confirmed companion experiment, held-out accuracy increased from 78 to 85 percent. What makes the project special is the visible experimental progression: data, tensors, architecture, individual predictions, model diversity, ensemble probabilities, and image-level error review all remain inspectable inside one reproducible notebook.
